relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: Capsaicin is a potent agonist of the TRPV1 channel, a transduction channel that is highly expressed in nociceptive fibers (pain fibers) throughout the peripheral nervous system.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: Ca2+ influx into the nociceptive terminal activates calpains, and Ca2+-dependent proteases, which is ultimately associated with disruption of the axonal cytoskeletal proteins [19].

relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: At week 12, greater decreases in the AUC for pain with walking was observed with capsaicin in the 0.5 and 1.0 mg groups versus placebo

key_findings: Capsaicin reversibly disrupts TRPV1-expressing nociceptor terminals rather than just blocking the channel.
Phase 2 intra-articular capsaicin (1 mg) reduced knee OA pain with walking versus placebo through 24 weeks.
